note: The canonical background-image prompt. The builder fetches and renders this, so improving the prompt reaches every author without releasing the builder. Keep `fixed` short and absolute: those rules are the ones that make a picture usable as an office.

theme.label: Theme
theme.help: What the place is. The single biggest decision, and the one a preset fills.

style.label: Style
style.help: How it is drawn. Flat vector reads best at small sizes; painted illustration has more character.
style.default: clean flat vector illustration, soft shadows, isometric-leaning top-down view

palette.label: Palette
palette.help: Keep it muted. The product draws avatars, room bars and status dots on top, and they need to win.
palette.default: muted warm neutrals with one cool accent

lighting.label: Lighting
lighting.help: Even light keeps every room equally readable. Dramatic light makes half the office hard to use.
lighting.default: even, diffuse daylight with no strong highlights

areaNames.label: Areas to draw
areaNames.help: Name the distinct areas you want, in the order you want them laid out. One reception and one break room are required.
areaNames.default: a reception by the entrance, a break room with a sofa and a coffee point, three work areas of different sizes, and two enclosed meeting rooms

entryEdge.label: Entry edge
entryEdge.help: Which edge the front door sits on. Reception goes here, so people arrive where the picture says they arrive.

fixed: Top-down floor plan of a single floor, seen from directly above, filling the whole frame edge to edge with no border, frame, margin or drop shadow around the image.
No text, no lettering, no numbers, no signage and no labels anywhere in the image. The product draws every room name itself, on top.
No people, no avatars and no figures. The product draws the people.
Draw the seats: chairs, sofas and stools where someone would sit, so the areas read as places to be rather than empty rectangles.
Nothing tall on desks or tables. No monitors standing up, no plants above seat height, no partitions that hide a seat from above, because an avatar has to sit on that surface and still be visible.
Areas are clearly separated by walls, floor colour or rugs, and are of deliberately different sizes: a big open area, some small ones.
Leave the floor inside each area relatively plain and uncluttered. Detail belongs at the edges, against the walls.
No vignette, no colour grading at the corners and no lens effects, because the product places rooms right up to the canvas edge.
template:
A {{shape}} ({{ratio}}) top-down floor plan of {{theme}}, at {{resolution}}.

Style: {{style}}.
Palette: {{palette}}.
Lighting: {{lighting}}.

Lay out: {{areaNames}}. The entrance and reception are on {{entryEdge}}.

Rules:
{{fixed}}
guidance: Use this prompt with an image model, or hand it to an illustrator; either works, and the rules matter more than the tool.
One reception and one break room. Both are required, and a template starts with them already placed.
Make the areas different sizes. An office where every room is the same size is dull to look at and tells nobody anything.
Generate a light version first. If you want a dark one, ask for the same scene recoloured, never a different layout, because both images share one set of room coordinates.
Check the result by looking at the middle of each area: could an avatar with a name label sit there and still be read? If not, ask for less clutter on the floor.

modern-office.label: Modern office
modern-office.theme: a modern open-plan office with exposed ceilings and warm wood floors
modern-office.style: clean flat vector illustration, soft shadows, isometric-leaning top-down view
modern-office.palette: muted warm neutrals with one teal accent
modern-office.lighting: even, diffuse daylight with no strong highlights
modern-office.areaNames: a reception with a desk and two armchairs by the entrance, a break room with a sofa and a coffee point, three work areas of different sizes with desks and chairs, and two enclosed glass meeting rooms

space-station.label: Space station
space-station.theme: a rotating space station deck with curved bulkheads and viewports onto starfield
space-station.style: clean flat vector illustration with subtle panel linework, top-down view
space-station.palette: cool graphite and off-white with cyan running lights
space-station.lighting: even artificial light, faint cyan glow from the floor strips
space-station.areaNames: an airlock reception at the entrance, a galley break area with a curved bench, three crew work bays of different sizes, and two enclosed briefing pods

rocket.label: Rocket
rocket.theme: a cutaway of a crewed rocket interior across several decks

rocket.areaNames: a hatch reception at the base, a galley break deck, three crew decks of different sizes with couches and consoles, and two enclosed comms cabins
